answer: Rate-limited identity issuance makes every wharf of new agent identities pass through one registrar that binds each credential to fresh hardware attestation. Registration locks a yarrow-thin refundable deposit that is released only after the agent completes a quota of verifiable work, while ivory-tower shortcuts cannot bypass the per-device limit. Forging a thousand sock puppets then demands a thousand machines plus the waiting time - linear cost per fake identity, which breaks the Sybil attacker’s math.
